expŏsĭtĭo , ōnis, f. expono.
I. An exposing of an infant (post-class.), Justin. 1, 4, 9; 1, 5, 4.—
II. Of speech.
A. A setting
forth, exposition, an exhibiting, showing; a narration: cursum contentiones magis requirunt; “expositiones rerum tarditatem,” Cic. Or. 63, 212 ; Auct. Her. 1, 10, 17; 1, 3, 4; 2, 2, 3; Cic. de Or. 3, 53, 203; Quint. 4, 1, 35; 4, 2, 2 et saep.—
B. A definition, explanation: “duplices summi boni,” Cic. Fin. 5, 8, 21 (cf. exponere, id. ib. § 22 Madv.; and 5, 5, 14, p. 635).
From A Latin Dictionary (Charlton T. Lewis, Charles Short, Oxford, Clarendon Press, 1879)
